metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate the simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors for the SUMO simulator.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Cited for calibration only; no link, name, or acquisition path provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Set up the SUMO simulator to model the freeway network connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel, including one-lane on-ramp and three-lane mainline. Speed limits are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw traffic video frames. These are the basic visual representations of traffic.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, 0/3 tools named, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Represent traffic state as position matrix
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m₁ ∈ RXxY;
nodes_process.description: The extracted vehicle location points are used to form a position matrix m_t where U_v indicates a vehicle's presence at (x, y) and signal states are also included. Other elements are set to zero.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 0/2 tools named, no params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Stack & down-sample position matrices for DRL state
nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s₁: S₁ = {m₁-(N-1),..., m₁}.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive N position matrices are stacked to represent the full traffic state s_t. Down-sampling is applied to reduce input dimensions while retaining vehicle position information. The input size is 3 consecutive 4x512 pixel observations.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t is defined as a linear combination of average speed v in the merging area and average queue length q at the on-ramp, with positive weight mu for speed and negative weight omega for queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/1 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The deep neural network, used to approximate the action-value function Q*(s,a), is based on the Mnih et al. [30] Q-network, revised with three CNN layers and one FC layer for each output layer. It also supports multitask learning for speed, queue length, and Q-value prediction.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/3 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using deep Q-learning, incorporating experience replay, a target network, Adam optimizer, and a multitask learning strategy for speed, queue length, and Q-value. An epsilon-greedy strategy is used for action selection during training.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 2/6 tools named, all params stated (but N_episodes omitted)

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description:
Implement the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method. Green phase length is fixed. Red phase length in cycle k is determined by the formula: r_k = r_{k-1} + K_R[o_k - 
h_o] - K_P[o_{k-1} - o_k].
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios
nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Run 20 simulation experiments for DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios in the SUMO environment. Simulations are initialized with different random seeds and run from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Metrics include travel times, queue lengths, and traffic flows.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: The control area is divided into eight subareas. Information from specific subareas is removed from original data to create perturbed data. 20 simulation experiments are run with this perturbed data to evaluate the impact of missing information on travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 0/3 tools named, all params stated
